problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=6+2t \\ y=5+t \\ z=-3-3t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:5x+3y-4z=-43.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Intersection Between a Line and a Plane

feedback.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=3-5t \\ y=2-3t \\ z=-2-6t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:5x-2y+4z-132=0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-2y+4z-132 & =0 \\ 5(3-5t)-2(2-3t)+4(-2-6t) & =132 \\ 15-25t-4+6t-8-24t & =132 \\ -43t & =129 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-5(-3)=18 \\ y=2-3(-3)=11 \\ z=-2-6(-3)=16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(18,11,16).$
